bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, execution-focused, deliberately conservative on guidance (acknowledged pattern of low-balling). Disciplined "stay focused" stance — explicitly declined to enter PCB/component manufacturing (chemical business, needs scale, low PCB cost share <teens) despite peer ECMS moves. Emphasis on ROCE/asset-turn discipline over chasing greenfield. Credible: delivered 46% vs 40% guide, doubling ~1 yr early.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- US factory is a **customer-acquisition funnel**, not a profit center — wins start in US then transition to India, where the margin is actually booked; plant-wise P&L understates US strategic value.
- Tariff episode was a net positive for funnel — accelerated US program wins as customers diversified supply chains.
- Box-build mix (56%) is the structural margin/stickiness story more than headline growth.
- Explicitly NOT pursuing PCB/component backward integration — differentiates from ECMS-chasing peers; PCB is <"teens" % of cost so vertical integration there is non-accretive.
- Semiconductor equipment win positions Avalon on the ISM 2.0 capital-equipment localization theme (rare for an EMS player).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Vertically integrated one-stop-shop: design, engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, assembly, testing and logistics on one platform, covering PCB design, PCBA, cable assembly and wire harnesses, sheet metal fabrication and machining, injection-moulded plastics, magnetics and end-to-end box-build
- Dual-shore India and U.S. manufacturing lets customers start in the U.S. and transition to India as volumes grow, giving flexibility on production allocation and customer proximity
- Diversification across industrials, mobility, clean energy, communications, medical and defence reduces concentration risk - management states no single vertical or customer carried FY2026
- Move up the complexity ladder: box-build rose from 44% to 54% of revenue over four years, deepening integration with customers and reducing handoffs
- Breadth of international quality accreditations (AS 9100, IATF 16949, ISO 13485, Nadcap) qualifying it for mission-critical aerospace, rail and medical programs
- Capex-light operating model, with management describing asset turns near 10x in FY2026

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration risk — A significant proportion of revenue is derived from a limited number of customers, so the loss of a key customer, a reduction in order volumes, a change in customer procurement strategy or termination of commercial arrangements could cause revenue volatility and adversely affect business performance. Avalon mitigates by broadening its customer base across industries and end markets and deepening long-term relationships through integrated manufacturing solutions.
- Raw material availability, quality and cost risk — Metals, electronic components, polymers and specialised inputs are critical to manufacturing; price volatility from supply-chain disruption, geopolitical developments, trade policy changes or supplier concentration can raise procurement costs and compress margins, while shortages or delays in critical materials can disrupt production schedules and order fulfilment. Mitigated through strategic sourcing across multiple suppliers and geographies, long-term procurement arrangements and evaluation of alternative materials.
- Currency fluctuation risk — Global operations and cross-border transactions expose the Company to U.S. Dollar, Euro and other currency movements that affect revenue realisation, import costs and profitability; unhedged exposures can produce foreign exchange losses in volatile periods. Managed through natural hedging of foreign-currency inflows and outflows, forward contracts and other derivatives, multi-currency invoicing and pricing adjustment mechanisms in long-term contracts.
- Macroeconomic risk — An economic slowdown, elevated inflation and other adverse macroeconomic conditions could reduce demand for electronics products and EMS services and disrupt import and export activity, affecting business volumes and operational performance. The Company also flags an unpredictable external environment shaped by wars, tariffs, supply-chain disruptions and trade realignments.
- Regulatory and incentive-scheme risk — Changes in laws, regulations or statutory requirements, or any non-compliance, could affect operations, business prospects and reputation; regulatory benefits and incentive schemes available to the industry may be delayed, modified or withdrawn, impacting business and financial performance. Diversification across products, markets and revenue streams reduces reliance on any single regulatory incentive.
- Operational and supply-chain execution risk — Disruptions in manufacturing processes, supply chain inefficiencies, equipment breakdowns, quality control issues, IT system failures or workforce-related challenges could cause production interruptions, delays in order fulfilment, higher operating costs, regulatory non-compliance and reputational impact. Mitigated through documented SOPs, automation and workforce development, periodic audits and lean manufacturing and Six Sigma practices.
- Cross-border trade and tariff exposure — The Company describes itself as having global operations and cross-border transactions, and flags that adverse macroeconomic developments may impact its import and export activities, potentially affecting business volumes and operational performance; trade policy changes are also named as a source of raw-material price volatility.

outlook.body:
- Evolve from an integrated manufacturing partner into a deeply embedded, end-to-end technology and manufacturing partner, engaging customers from early product development through concept, prototyping and commercial production
- Move up the complexity ladder within EMS - taking on harder, higher-value box-build and mission-critical programs rather than commodity assembly; box-build has risen from 44% to 54% of revenue over four years
- Blend of geography: cater to the world's fastest-growing EMS markets, India and the USA, harnessing India manufacturing and USA onboarding under the dual-shore model
- Combination of existing and new technologies: deepen presence in industrial, aero, rail and communication segments through collaboration, up-selling and cross-selling to increase wallet share, while expanding into emerging advanced-technology sectors by partnering with industry pioneers
- Balance profitability and growth: focus on profitable segments such as aerospace, complex and mission-critical products and box-builds, and win new orders through integrated design-to-box-build capabilities
- Build a semiconductor manufacturing equipment vertical, working as a qualified external partner to global equipment manufacturers on complex Industry 4.0-compliant assemblies
- Integrate manufacturing, logistics, warehousing and supply-chain capabilities so customers get better visibility and delivery, expanding Avalon's role from manufacturing partner to strategic partner across a broader part of the value chain
- Diversify customers and geographies - expanding presence in Europe and Southeast Asia and adding customers across industrial and defence segments to reduce concentration
- Maintain a capex-light model with high asset turns while continuing to invest in capabilities
- Automate the finance function - OCR-based invoice processing, a financial consolidation and reporting tool replacing manual Excel processes, and host-to-host digital payments for imports
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Avalon runs a capex-light expansion model built on a dual-shore footprint of 15 facilities across India and the United States, with over 575K+ sq. ft. of design and production space and 65 production lines carrying built-in buffer capacity to ramp up production. On a standalone basis the BRSR reports 5 plants and 1 office in India, spread across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, with the Chennai facilities located inside a Special Economic Zone and equipped for large-scale box-build programs, specialised metal processing and expanded plastics manufacturing; the U.S. Atlanta operations are automation-led and focused on system integration and end-product configuration, while Bengaluru adds design and manufacturing capability. Expansion in FY2026 came through capability build-out rather than large greenfield projects: the Company expanded manufacturing and engineering capabilities through capacity additions and strategic technology collaborations, launched manufacturing of semiconductor equipment, advanced electronic systems and high-end complex box-build solutions, and secured AS9100D and IPC A-610 J / A-600 K / WHMA-A-620 E certifications. Programme-level ramps under way include energy storage system (BESS) programs continuing to ramp as planned, commencement of locomotive engine subsystem production, aerospace cabin sub-assemblies moving through validation towards volume production, the Railway Kavach anti-collision system completing testing and progressing towards commercial production, and satellite communication control-unit prototypes with volume orders expected to commence in FY2027. The semiconductor manufacturing equipment partnership with a leading global player reached project readiness in FY2026, with volume production expected from FY2027. Prior-year steps in the Company's own timeline include investment in two new plants and partnerships such as Zepco in 2025. Management states it maintained a capex-light model with asset turns near 10x and continues to focus on investments in advanced manufacturing, high-value box-build solutions, precision engineering and capacity expansion initiatives, alongside expansion of market presence into Europe and Southeast Asia.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects the shift of the revenue mix further towards India manufacturing over the next 18 to 24 months to bring operating leverage and improve the blended consolidated margin profile; India manufacturing currently runs at EBITDA margins of 16.7%
- Growth is supported by three key pillars - expansion of existing customer relationships, new business wins across verticals, and conversion of a strong opportunity pipeline into production programs
- Structural tailwinds in clean energy, railways, aerospace, industrial automation and defence; progress in energy storage systems (BESS), railway safety systems including Kavach, advanced aerospace components and communication solutions is expected to support future growth
- Entry into the semiconductor equipment segment is described as a significant long-term opportunity, with validations progressing and volume production expected from FY2027
- Several new programs enter FY2027 in active production or at the cusp of it, with contribution building through the year; management is appropriately cautious about the time new programs take to fully ramp
- Global supply-chain diversification and friend-shoring (China+1 as an active procurement strategy) strengthen India and the U.S. as manufacturing hubs, favouring Avalon's dual-shore footprint and customers' preference for geographically resilient sourcing
- India's FTA push into Europe and the concluded India-EU Free Trade Agreement are opening new doors for export competitiveness
- Semiconductor supply chain restructuring across Asia, plus India's ISM 2.0 with a total budget outlay of Rs 1,27,500 Cr, aligns with Avalon's recent wins in semiconductor equipment manufacturing
- Indian EMS demand is underpinned by PLI, SPECS, EMC 2.0 and Design Linked Incentive schemes and by rising electronics content across automotive, telecom, data centres and industrial automation
- Tariff cost pressure was passed through to customers substantially in full when tariffs spiked during the year, protecting margins
- Diversified end-market exposure limited the impact of sharply higher memory prices, given the focus on industrial and other diversified applications and the small contribution of memory components to the bill of materials
- Indian manufacturing operations accounted for 79% of revenue in FY2026, serving both domestic and global clients
- Management cautions that the external environment will remain unpredictable - wars, tariffs, supply-chain disruptions and trade realignment make planning harder
- Avalon enters FY2027 with a healthy order book of Rs 2,196 Cr, new programs entering production and a pipeline that continues to grow
- Maintained strong order visibility with an order book of Rs 2,196 Cr and long-term contracts of Rs 1,245 Cr
- Broad-based new business secured across rail, aerospace, industrial, clean energy, power, communications, semiconductor equipment and satellite communications, with several programs progressing from design and prototyping into production and volume ramp-up
- Three large U.S.-based customers were added during the year, with programs progressing from prototype to commercialization

one-line thesis: A focused, capex-light, high-end box-build EMS compounding ~45% over 7 straight quarters with improving margins/ROCE (20.6%), now adding three structural growth engines (energy storage, aerospace sub-assemblies, semiconductor equipment) that should sustain a guided second revenue doubling to ~INR3,200 cr by FY29.

One-offs: ~110 bps optical GM% drag from tariff pass-through (volume-neutral); other income boosted by forex gain. US manufacturing loss narrowed to ~INR5 cr in Q4 (from ~INR14 cr/qtr two years ago).
guidance (verify next quarter):
- **FY27 revenue growth: 24%–27%** (explicitly "conservative"; last year started at 18–20% and delivered 46%).
- **3-year frame: ~INR3,200 cr by FY29** (second doubling off INR1,603 cr base). Already ~1 yr ahead on the original FY24→FY27 doubling (~INR1,725 cr target).
- US manufacturing breakeven targeted **later part of FY27**.
- Gross margin band reaffirmed **33%–35%**. No explicit EBITDA% guidance ("operating leverage scope" only).
- India:US mix to stay ~78:22 to 80:20.
- Mgmt declined quarterly revenue guidance (no 1Q seasonality claimed).
order book & pipeline:
- Total INR3,441 cr: INR2,196 cr executable in 12–14 months (+24.7% YoY) and INR1,245 cr executable 14–36 months; further >3-yr orders excluded.
- Growth broad-based across verticals and geographies. Three large US customers (industrial + defence) onboarded last quarter moving prototype→production.
- New geographies opening: Southeast Asia exports expanding; Europe sales presence building (aligned with India-Europe trade deal).
- Aerospace: increasing interest from majors; pursuing advanced metal cockpit assemblies and landing-gear components (new areas).
segment / subsidiary:
- **Industrial** ~34% of rev, +65% YoY (fastest).
- **Mobility** ~28%, +50% (rail 16%, aerospace 9%).
- **Clean energy** ~20%, +45% (energy storage systems ramp).
- **Communications** ~8%, +58%.
- Geography: India mfg ~77% of Q4 rev (EBITDA margin 16.7%, PAT margin 12.2%); US mfg ~23% (Q4 loss ~INR5 cr, narrowing). FY26 mix India 79% / US 21%; India biz +33% FY26, US +59%.
- Box-build now 56% of mix (vs 44% four years ago) — higher integration, stickiness, margin.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Energy storage systems** — ramping in line with plan (drives clean-energy growth).
- **Aerospace cabin sub-assemblies** — passed first article inspection, moving to volume; plus optionality in cockpit assemblies/landing gear.
- **Locomotive engine subsystems** — production commenced.
- **Kavach anti-collision** — testing complete, on track for commercial production.
- **Semiconductor manufacturing equipment** — completed project-readiness phase with a global partner; ~50–60% of part numbers cleared awaiting production approval, rest in progress; volume from FY27; intended to spin into a separate vertical over 2–3 yrs (ISM 2.0 tailwind).
- **Satcom control units** — first prototype tranche done; volume orders expected FY27.
- Industrial processing & power-sector customer prototypes commenced.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Q4 EBITDA 11.8% (up from 11.5% Q3); FY26 10.8%. India ops already at 16.7% EBITDA / 12.2% PAT — drag is loss-making US ops.
- Margin levers: (i) US breakeven in late FY27 + post-breakeven leverage; (ii) rising box-build share; (iii) operating leverage on scale. No quantified EBITDA target (peers cited at ~16%).
- Tariffs fully passed through — protected absolute GM but optically diluted GM% ~110 bps. PCB/raw-material price spikes also passed through.
capex / expansion:
- Capex-light: Q4 INR21 cr; FY26 INR56 cr (FY25 INR58 cr). Guidance ~INR50–60 cr/yr, "maybe a little over."
- Asset turns ~9.9x; targets 8–10x. No major capex foreseen near-term despite planned doubling — most capex is buildings/infrastructure.
capital allocation:
- ROCE 20.6% (from 15.7% a yr ago, 10% two yrs ago); stated aspiration >20%, longer-term march back toward historical ~25%.
- Net debt INR40 cr (total debt INR183 cr, cash/investments INR143 cr); net debt/equity 0.06.
- FCF inflection: CFO INR57 cr FY26 vs INR25 cr FY25, driven by working-capital improvement.
- NWC 112 days (from 124 days; better than 120–130 guidance); receivables 72d (from 84d), inventory 84d (from 86d), payables 45d.
risks & watch-items:
- US manufacturing still loss-making (~INR5 cr Q4); breakeven only "later part of FY27" — execution risk.
- Customer concentration: top 10 = 61% of FY26 revenue.
- Large-program timing lumpiness (cut-in quarter controlled by customer) — basis for conservative guidance.
- Geopolitics / tariffs / Middle-East driven PCB supply tightness & pricing (mitigated by pass-through and active inventory management, but flagged as fluid).
- FY27 guidance (24–27%) is a sharp deceleration vs 46% — base effect; watch for beats vs guidance pattern.
- Semiconductor vertical is long-gestation; revenue contribution still unquantified.
management quality / tone: Confident, execution-focused, deliberately conservative on guidance (acknowledged pattern of low-balling). Disciplined "stay focused" stance — explicitly declined to enter PCB/component manufacturing (chemical business, needs scale, low PCB cost share <teens) despite peer ECMS moves. Emphasis on ROCE/asset-turn discipline over chasing greenfield. Credible: delivered 46% vs 40% guide, doubling ~1 yr early.
non-obvious takeaways:
- US factory is a **customer-acquisition funnel**, not a profit center — wins start in US then transition to India, where the margin is actually booked; plant-wise P&L understates US strategic value.
- Tariff episode was a net positive for funnel — accelerated US program wins as customers diversified supply chains.
- Box-build mix (56%) is the structural margin/stickiness story more than headline growth.
- Explicitly NOT pursuing PCB/component backward integration — differentiates from ECMS-chasing peers; PCB is <"teens" % of cost so vertical integration there is non-accretive.
- Semiconductor equipment win positions Avalon on the ISM 2.0 capital-equipment localization theme (rare for an EMS player).

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Avalon is a fully integrated EMS provider offering end-to-end solutions across the value chain, from PCB design and assembly through to complete electronic systems (box-build), with in-house cable assembly, wire harnesses, sheet metal fabrication, machining, injection-moulded plastics and magnetics. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects the shift of the revenue mix further towards India manufacturing over the next 18 to 24 months to bring operating leverage and improve the blended consolidated margin profile; India manufacturing currently runs at EBITDA margins of 16.7%
- Growth is supported by three key pillars - expansion of existing customer relationships, new business wins across verticals, and conversion of a strong opportunity pipeline into production programs
- Structural tailwinds in clean energy, railways, aerospace, industrial automation and defence; progress in energy storage systems (BESS), railway safety systems including Kavach, advanced aerospace components and communication solutions is expected to support future growth
- Entry into the semiconductor equipment segment is described as a significant long-term opportunity, with validations progressing and volume production expected from FY2027
- Several new programs enter FY2027 in active production or at the cusp of it, with contribution building through the year; management is appropriately cautious about the time new programs take to fully ramp
- Global supply-chain diversification and friend-shoring (China+1 as an active procurement strategy) strengthen India and the U.S. as manufacturing hubs, favouring Avalon's dual-shore footprint and customers' preference for geographically resilient sourcing
- India's FTA push into Europe and the concluded India-EU Free Trade Agreement are opening new doors for export competitiveness
- Semiconductor supply chain restructuring across Asia, plus India's ISM 2.0 with a total budget outlay of Rs 1,27,500 Cr, aligns with Avalon's recent wins in semiconductor equipment manufacturing
- Indian EMS demand is underpinned by PLI, SPECS, EMC 2.0 and Design Linked Incentive schemes and by rising electronics content across automotive, telecom, data centres and industrial automation
- Tariff cost pressure was passed through to customers substantially in full when tariffs spiked during the year, protecting margins
- Diversified end-market exposure limited the impact of sharply higher memory prices, given the focus on industrial and other diversified applications and the small contribution of memory components to the bill of materials
- Indian manufacturing operations accounted for 79% of revenue in FY2026, serving both domestic and global clients
- Management cautions that the external environment will remain unpredictable - wars, tariffs, supply-chain disruptions and trade realignment make planning harder
- Avalon enters FY2027 with a healthy order book of Rs 2,196 Cr, new programs entering production and a pipeline that continues to grow
- Maintained strong order visibility with an order book of Rs 2,196 Cr and long-term contracts of Rs 1,245 Cr
- Broad-based new business secured across rail, aerospace, industrial, clean energy, power, communications, semiconductor equipment and satellite communications, with several programs progressing from design and prototyping into production and volume ramp-up
- Three large U.S.-based customers were added during the year, with programs progressing from prototype to commercialization

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Avalon runs a capex-light expansion model built on a dual-shore footprint of 15 facilities across India and the United States, with over 575K+ sq. ft. of design and production space and 65 production lines carrying built-in buffer capacity to ramp up production. On a standalone basis the BRSR reports 5 plants and 1 office in India, spread across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, with the Chennai facilities located inside a Special Economic Zone and equipped for large-scale box-build programs, specialised metal processing and expanded plastics manufacturing; the U.S. Atlanta operations are automation-led and focused on system integration and end-product configuration, while Bengaluru adds design and manufacturing capability. Expansion in FY2026 came through capability build-out rather than large greenfield projects: the Company expanded manufacturing and engineering capabilities through capacity additions and strategic technology collaborations, launched manufacturing of semiconductor equipment, advanced electronic systems and high-end complex box-build solutions, and secured AS9100D and IPC A-610 J / A-600 K / WHMA-A-620 E certifications. Programme-level ramps under way include energy storage system (BESS) programs continuing to ramp as planned, commencement of locomotive engine subsystem production, aerospace cabin sub-assemblies moving through validation towards volume production, the Railway Kavach anti-collision system completing testing and progressing towards commercial production, and satellite communication control-unit prototypes with volume orders expected to commence in FY2027. The semiconductor manufacturing equipment partnership with a leading global player reached project readiness in FY2026, with volume production expected from FY2027. Prior-year steps in the Company's own timeline include investment in two new plants and partnerships such as Zepco in 2025. Management states it maintained a capex-light model with asset turns near 10x and continues to focus on investments in advanced manufacturing, high-value box-build solutions, precision engineering and capacity expansion initiatives, alongside expansion of market presence into Europe and Southeast Asia.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, execution-focused, deliberately conservative on guidance (acknowledged pattern of low-balling). Disciplined "stay focused" stance — explicitly declined to enter PCB/component manufacturing (chemical business, needs scale, low PCB cost share <teens) despite peer ECMS moves. Emphasis on ROCE/asset-turn discipline over chasing greenfield. Credible: delivered 46% vs 40% guide, doubling ~1 yr early.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated one-stop-shop: design, engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, assembly, testing and logistics on one platform, covering PCB design, PCBA, cable assembly and wire harnesses, sheet metal fabrication and machining, injection-moulded plastics, magnetics and end-to-end box-build
- Dual-shore India and U.S. manufacturing lets customers start in the U.S. and transition to India as volumes grow, giving flexibility on production allocation and customer proximity
- Diversification across industrials, mobility, clean energy, communications, medical and defence reduces concentration risk - management states no single vertical or customer carried FY2026
- Move up the complexity ladder: box-build rose from 44% to 54% of revenue over four years, deepening integration with customers and reducing handoffs
- Breadth of international quality accreditations (AS 9100, IATF 16949, ISO 13485, Nadcap) qualifying it for mission-critical aerospace, rail and medical programs
- Capex-light operating model, with management describing asset turns near 10x in FY2026
- Customer relationships strong enough that when tariffs spiked during the year the Company passed through substantially all of the impact to customers
- Credit profile strengthened during the year from A-/Stable outlook to A-/Positive outlook rating

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- US manufacturing still loss-making (~INR5 cr Q4); breakeven only "later part of FY27" — execution risk.
- Customer concentration: top 10 = 61% of FY26 revenue.
- Large-program timing lumpiness (cut-in quarter controlled by customer) — basis for conservative guidance.
- Geopolitics / tariffs / Middle-East driven PCB supply tightness & pricing (mitigated by pass-through and active inventory management, but flagged as fluid).
- FY27 guidance (24–27%) is a sharp deceleration vs 46% — base effect; watch for beats vs guidance pattern.
- Semiconductor vertical is long-gestation; revenue contribution still unquantified.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- US factory is a **customer-acquisition funnel**, not a profit center — wins start in US then transition to India, where the margin is actually booked; plant-wise P&L understates US strategic value.
- Tariff episode was a net positive for funnel — accelerated US program wins as customers diversified supply chains.
- Box-build mix (56%) is the structural margin/stickiness story more than headline growth.
- Explicitly NOT pursuing PCB/component backward integration — differentiates from ECMS-chasing peers; PCB is <"teens" % of cost so vertical integration there is non-accretive.
- Semiconductor equipment win positions Avalon on the ISM 2.0 capital-equipment localization theme (rare for an EMS player).

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Evolve from an integrated manufacturing partner into a deeply embedded, end-to-end technology and manufacturing partner, engaging customers from early product development through concept, prototyping and commercial production
- Move up the complexity ladder within EMS - taking on harder, higher-value box-build and mission-critical programs rather than commodity assembly; box-build has risen from 44% to 54% of revenue over four years
- Blend of geography: cater to the world's fastest-growing EMS markets, India and the USA, harnessing India manufacturing and USA onboarding under the dual-shore …
